question: can the decision layer use patient age more finely than three bands?

objective.constraint_handling: hinge penalty x10.0 inside the optimiser (A4-A6); hard filter on the grid (A1-A3, A7 local fits)

age_representation.missing_age: the arm's pooled lambda (never an estimated age)

coverage_regime: full coverage (declared deviation D2, see module docstring)

deviations.D1: A6 is optimised on the S5 objective with a P-spline ridge penalty; sklearn Ridge is used only for the warm start (no squared-error response exists).
deviations.D2: fitted at full coverage, not on S56's referral regime (budget does not transfer).
deviations.D3: A4/A5 are linear/quadratic in the softplus link, so lambda >= 0 holds.
deviations.D4: every fitted arm is floor-repaired per band (repair_floor) so all arms carry A1's constraint; A3's kernel-weighted floor and A7's unconstrained shrinkage do not.
deviations.D5: AP (one pooled lambda) is a CV reference outside the family, not floor-repaired.

dependency_graph.Dirichlet_deployed: fit on all OOF rows; scores val and reserved
dependency_graph.Dirichlet_k: fit on OOF folds != k; scores OOF fold k (S5 cross-fit)
dependency_graph.lambda_reported: fit on Dirichlet_k outputs over all folds (in-sample for lambda)
dependency_graph.cv_fold_k: lambda fit on folds != k with an inner cross-fit over those folds; fold k scored by a map fit on folds != k
dependency_graph.for_S57b: cross-fit lambda itself with this nesting; no row may be scored by an age function or calibrator fitted on it

audit_item_1_gate_on_5_year_bins.fallback: pooled lambda fitted on all rows (fit_lambda_by_group)
